title.tagline: Train your voice, at your pace
title.description: Analyze 5 voice metrics in real time and score them against your voice type. A browser-only voice training app.
title.feature1: Set goals across pitch, quality, and intonation
title.feature2: Recording and analysis stay on your device
title.privacyNote: Audio is never sent to a server

settings.title: Voice Type Settings
settings.subtitle: Choose the type of feminine voice you want to train
settings.profileSubtitle: Start with one of these four feminine voice types. Choose custom if you want to tune each parameter yourself.
settings.lockedProfileDescription: This profile uses fixed targets so progress stays comparable. Choose Custom if you want to change the axes manually.

natural.name: Natural
natural.description: A practical, natural, easy-to-understand feminine voice. The standard choice if you are not sure where to start.

soft.name: Soft
soft.description: A gentle, calm, warm feminine voice. Good if you want a lower voice that still reads feminine.

cute.name: Cute
cute.description: A bright, slightly higher, cute feminine voice. A good fit for singing or streaming practice.

cool.name: Cool
cool.description: A clear, polished voice with less sweetness. Good if you want a calm, mature impression.

custom.name: Custom
custom.description: Adjust pitch, quality, and intonation yourself. Custom sessions stay in the list, but are excluded from comparison charts.

practice.title: Practice
practice.subtitle: Tap the mic button to record your voice
practice.phraseSubtitle: Each voice type has a phrase set designed for more consistent comparison. Read both sentences continuously when recording.
practice.formantNotice: Formants, spectral centroid, and HNR are reference values. They vary by vowel and phonation, so compare against literature-based profile targets.
practice.needSettings: Please configure your voice type first

formantReferences.custom: Reference vowel for the selected pitch range

qualityReferences.natural: Moderate brightness, relatively clear (near average female speech)
qualityReferences.cute: Brighter tone; light breathiness is acceptable
qualityReferences.custom: Reference values for the selected quality type

metricDescriptions.f0: The center of your pitch. A higher score means your voice is staying close to the selected pitch range.
metricDescriptions.formantF1: A lower resonance component affected by mouth opening and tongue position. This reference value varies strongly by vowel.
metricDescriptions.formantF2: A higher resonance component affected by tongue placement. Brighter, more front vowels tend to raise this reference value.
metricDescriptions.spectralCentroid: A reference for vocal brightness, averaged from voiced frames. It varies with vowel and level.
metricDescriptions.hnr: A reference for harmonic-to-noise ratio. It reflects breathiness and varies with phonation.
metricDescriptions.intonation: The pitch movement range during the recording. Larger values indicate more expression, while smaller values can sound flatter.

metricTips.f0: Avoid squeezing your throat. Start short phrases slightly below the target, then gradually move closer.
metricTips.formant: Try a slight smile, a more forward tongue position, and smaller, cleaner vowel shapes.
metricTips.spectralCentroid: For a brighter sound, aim resonance toward the front of the mouth. If it becomes harsh, reduce excess air pressure.
metricTips.hnr: Use less breath leakage and practice sustaining a light, steady tone.
metricTips.intonation: Add small pitch movements across the whole phrase, then listen back for places that sound too flat.

feedback.onTarget: This is very close to the target. Try to remember how this placement felt and repeat it once more.

f0.high: Try landing the pitch a little lower while keeping the throat relaxed and the air moving forward.
f0.low: Imagine the voice stretching upward in a thin line, then place it just a little higher without pushing.

formantF1.high: Avoid opening the mouth too much and try shaping the vowel a little smaller.
formantF1.low: Create a little more vertical space in the mouth so the vowel does not get too compressed.

formantF2.high: The resonance may be too far forward. Keep some space farther back instead of making the sound only at the lips.
formantF2.low: Try a slight smile and a more forward tongue position to move toward a brighter vowel.

spectralCentroid.high: The sound is on the bright side. Use less air pressure and imagine a slightly rounder resonance.
spectralCentroid.low: The sound is on the darker side. Aim the resonance toward the front of the mouth and brighten it slightly.

hnr.high: The voice is clearer and less breathy than the target. If you want to match it, add a very light breathy layer.
hnr.low: There is more breath noise than the target. Imagine sustaining a thin, steady line instead of letting too much air escape.

intonation.high: The pitch movement is large. Try making a gentle slope instead of letting the ending jump too much.
intonation.low: The pitch movement is small. Add one small hill inside the phrase so it does not sound too flat.

history.title: Practice history
history.chartProfile: Recommended profile shown in the chart
history.customChartNotice: To keep comparisons meaningful, custom sessions are excluded from charts and remain available in the list and details.
history.formantChartNotice: Formants are vowel-dependent reference values. The dashed line is a literature-based target for the selected profile.
history.qualityChartNotice: Spectral centroid and HNR are phonation-dependent reference values. The dashed line is a literature-based target.
history.metricGuideIntro: The chart shows measured values over time. The dashed line is the target for each session.

metricGuide.total: A weighted score across all metrics. Start with the overall trend, then inspect which metric caused a drop.
metricGuide.f0: The center of your pitch. Use the chart to compare measured values against the target.
metricGuide.formant: A combined F1/F2 resonance score. Mouth opening, tongue position, and vowel shape are the main levers.
metricGuide.formantF1: Lower resonance affected by mouth opening and tongue position. The target is a representative vowel reference.
metricGuide.formantF2: Higher resonance affected by tongue placement. The target is a representative vowel reference.
metricGuide.spectralCentroid: A reference for vocal brightness. Values below the target tend to sound darker; values above tend to sound brighter.
metricGuide.hnr: A reference for breathiness. Values below the target suggest more breathiness; values above suggest a clearer tone.
metricGuide.intonation: Pitch movement across the phrase. Values below the target suggest a flatter delivery; values above suggest more movement.
